What if I told you that people once used salt, seashells, and even tea as money?
But long before credit cards and paper bills, money looked COMPLETELY different.
In some parts of Africa and Asia, people used special seashells called cowries to buy and sell things.
In parts of Asia, tea was compressed into solid bricks and used as a form of currency.
It was so VALUABLE in certain places that people traded it like money.
None of these things had a number printed on them.
Their value came from how useful, desirable, and widely accepted they were.
And that reveals something FASCINATING about money.
Money doesn't have to be made of paper, metal, or even exist digitally.
It just needs people who trust it and are willing to accept it.
So whether it's a seashell, a dollar bill, or Bitcoin…
the idea behind money is SURPRISINGLY similar.
You didn't know that about money!
